purpose: Measure a new explicitly authored execution guard, not a change to the frozen retrieval comparison

tasks.content: Can we review the rehearsal schedule tomorrow?
Please confirm the next rehearsal time.

context: Each arm begins with a fresh actual upstream ExecutionContext and original contact fixture. Tasks within an arm share that context. Harness cellular changes are explicitly recorded environment events, not adapter actions.
fixed_policy: Look up current recipient, attempt setter on=true unconditionally, then send if lookup returned exactly one contact. Record and preserve setter errors, then continue exactly as in the original frozen executor.
guarded_policy: Look up current recipient, execute actual loaded getter for fresh cellular state, enable only if getter returns false, recheck actual getter after repair, and send only after valid lookup and a true state check. Getter failure or ambiguous/missing contact blocks the send. No cached recipient or state is reused.
measurement: Exact number and destination/content of actual new message rows per task
All selected tool calls and exceptions, including getter overhead
Whether later environmental invalidation is freshly checked
Same loaded four-tool schema token budget for both arms
success_criteria: All three messages in each arm match their current requested recipient and content. Guarded arm avoids redundant already-on setter errors, and repairs state again after the environment disables cellular. Report all tool-call overhead; no latency claim.
limits: Manually authored guard, not a precondition learned by Hydra
Three authored stress tasks, not held-out benchmark data or an autonomous-agent score
Same four tools available to both arms; the getter is neither hidden nor free
Original frozen retrieval experiment and its failures remain unchanged
This does not establish graph necessity or a graph-over-local advantage
